key_insight: Controlled oxygen annealing can self-correct slightly Sr-rich epitaxial SrTiO3 on silicon by driving excess Sr out of the lattice through temperature-dependent segregation pathways.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable post-growth route to improve STO stoichiometry and crystalline quality for oxide-on-silicon integration, helping expand the usable process window beyond flux-limited MBE growth.
method: Grow intentionally Sr-rich epitaxial SrTiO3 on Si(001) by oxide molecular beam epitaxy.
Anneal the films in oxygen across a broad temperature range.
Track how excess Sr redistributes via surface outgrowths below 800 °C and interfacial SiO2 accumulation above 800 °C.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports broad-temperature annealing experiments that revealed two distinct Sr-segregation mechanisms and showed progressive removal of excess Sr from the STO lattice.
watch_item: High-temperature annealing may also thicken or alter the interfacial SiO2 layer, so integration must balance stoichiometry correction against interface preservation.
paper_title: Stoichiometric Epitaxial Strontium Titanate Thin Films on Silicon by High-Temperature Sr Segregation
